purpose: PROJECT_ASSESSMENT section 4.1 says the teaching simulator and the research infrastructure are decoupled and splitting them needs no refactor. This registry turns that from a claim into a checked fact: the teaching entry point's transitive local import closure must be exactly the modules listed here, so a research import cannot enter it unnoticed and the list cannot quietly go stale. Rules: docs/TEACHING_BOUNDARY.md.

notes.stable_baselines3: The teaching closure does import stable_baselines3, through controller_rl loading a PPO policy for the Live view. That is the teaching product doing its job, not a research dependency: the boundary is drawn around research MODULES, not around third-party weight.
notes.rl_package: backend/rl/ holds both sides. Two of its modules are teaching (policy_registry, training_inventory); the rest - train_ppo, eval_policy, humanoid_env, the runners and the protocol JSONs - are research and must stay out of the closure. A directory boundary would not have expressed this; an enumerated one does.

out_of_scope.tests: backend/test_*.py may import anything; a test is not the shipped application.
out_of_scope.third_party: Which PyPI packages the teaching product needs is a packaging question, not a boundary question, and is deliberately not checked here.
out_of_scope.frontend: The frontend reaches the backend only over the HTTP/WebSocket API, so it cannot import a research module; its surface is 5 REST paths and 2 sockets.
